'''Arnold Gay''' (born 11 May 1967) is a television presenter and former radio presenter from [[Singapore]]. He is currently presenting the breakfast show "Asia First" on [[CNA (TV network)|CNA]] together with Julie Yoo, Teresa Tang, Yasmin Jonkers, Elizabeth Neo & Sarah Al-Khaldi from Jan 2024. He previously worked at Singapore radio stations [[Class 95FM]], [[Power 98 (radio station)|Power 98 FM]], [[Kiss 92FM]], as well as sister channel [[CNA938]]. He was also a [[Broadcast journalism|broadcast journalist]] at various TV stations including [[CNA (TV network)|CNA]], [[CNBC Asia]], [[Bloomberg Television|Bloomberg TV]] and [[Reuters TV]].

== Education ==
Gay was educated at [[Catholic High School, Singapore|Catholic High School]], [[St. Joseph's Institution, Singapore|St Joseph's Institution]] and [[Raffles Junior College]], before going on to the [[National University of Singapore]] where he majored in Economics and [[Psychology]].

== Biography ==
Gay's first job in radio was as a presenter at [[Class 95FM]], where he subsequently became the station's music director. He then became the music director at the newly-opened [[Power 98 (radio station)|Power 98 FM]] in 1994.<ref>[http://www.asiaone.com/showbiz/arnold-gay-seriously-funny-guy Arnold Gay is a seriously funny guy], ''The Straits Times'', 15 July 2014.</ref>

Gay then moved into the television industry in 1995, becoming a music video programmer for [[Channel V]] in Hong Kong. In 1998, he returned to Singapore to become a news reporter at [[Channel NewsAsia]]. In December 2000, he moved to the new [[Singapore Press Holdings]]' division [[SPH MediaWorks]] television channel, [[Channel i (Singaporean TV channel)|TVWorks]], as a presenter on ''The Straits Times TV News'' (later renamed ''[[Channel i News]]'').<ref>{{cite web |date=1 December 2000 |title=News personalities join SPH as TV journalists |url=https://eresources.nlb.gov.sg/newspapers/digitised/article/straitstimes20001201-1.2.199.19 |access-date=13 September 2023 |website=The Straits Times (retrieved from NLB)}}</ref> When the channel folded at the end of 2004, he became an assistant news editor for the ''[[The Straits Times|Straits Times]]'' newspaper. In 2005, he became the Singapore Press Holdings Head of Corporate Relations.<ref>[http://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=24193299&ticker=SPH:SP&previousCapId=875569&previousTitle=Singapore%20Press%20Holdings%20Limited Singapore Press Holdings Ltd – Arnold Gay], Bloomberg L.P.. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref> He later moved back into broadcast journalism and had stints at [[CNBC Asia]], [[Bloomberg Television|Bloomberg TV]] and [[Reuters TV]].

In 2012, Gay returned to the radio industry to join the new Singapore radio station [[Kiss 92FM]]. Since the station opened in August 2012, he has been the co-host of the station's breakfast show, 'Maddy, Jason and Arnold in the Mornings', from 6.00 – 10.00 am on weekdays together with [[Maddy Barber]] and [[Jason Johnson (radio presenter)|Jason Johnson]] until March 2019.<ref>[http://www.asiaone.com/showbiz/kiss92-top-english-top-english-music-station Kiss92 is top English music station], ''The New Paper'', 20 June 2014.</ref><ref>[https://tnp.straitstimes.com/entertainment/m/kiss92-fms-morning-trio-breakfast-habits Kiss92 FM’s morning trio on breakfast habits], ''The New Paper'', 2 July 2014.</ref><ref>[http://www.sphradio.sg/portfolio_page/arnold-gay-kiss92-fm/ Arnold Gay, Kiss92 FM] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171015154002/http://www.sphradio.sg/portfolio_page/arnold-gay-kiss92-fm/ |date=15 October 2017 }}, SPH Radio. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref> He left the station (and return to his original employers [[Mediacorp]]) to host the breakfast show, "Asia First", with former [[Money FM 89.3]] DJ Yasmin Jonkers, on a revamped radio station, [[938Now|CNA938]] (previously 938Now) for 4 years from 2019 - 2023. 

At the start of 2024, he was promoted back as a Television Presenter on the main [[CNA (TV network)|CNA]] channel to anchor the TV version of the "Asia First" programme to be partnered mainly with Julie Yoo and Elizabeth Neo, replacing Steve Lai who had moved to [[BBC News (British TV channel)|BBC News]], thereby marking Gay's return to the television screens.

== Personal life ==
Gay has two brothers and one sister. His father was a Station Manager for [[British Airways]] and his mother was a bank officer.

Gay met his wife, Deborah Chia, when she was working as a DJ at Class 95FM. The couple have one son.
